note: Original Orbis factual synthesis; linked federal records and historic-site accounts, checked 14 October 2026. Points locate places approximately, not territorial extents. Modern national/state outlines are reference geography, never reconstructed historical borders. No archival images or source prose redistributed. St Charles: 16 May 1804, direct Clark journal quotation on https://www.nps.gov/places/st-charles-historic-district.htm preferred over contradictory May 14 summary/chronology.

items.title: New Orleans
items.text: The Louisiana Purchase treaty was signed in 1803. New Orleans locates the river port central to negotiations; this point does not stand for the purchase’s boundaries.

items.title: Across the continent
items.text: Lewis and Clark travelled west in 1804–1805. Move the dated slider through selected NPS-documented stops: St Charles, Rocheport, Three Forks and Cape Disappointment. The connecting route is schematic.

items.title: Santa Fe
items.text: Texas entered the United States in 1845. The war with Mexico ended with the 1848 Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo and a major territorial cession; Santa Fe locates one affected region, not the whole cession.

items.title: Columbia mouth
items.text: The Oregon Treaty of 1846 divided competing British and US claims in the Pacific Northwest. The point locates the Columbia mouth; it is not a treaty boundary.

items.title: Sitka / Alaska
items.text: The United States purchased Alaska from Russia in 1867. The acquisition preceded statehood by decades and did not mean that Alaska Native peoples had sold their own rights.
